Presidential debates are an agreement between several private parties (the candidates, the networks, and the Commission on Presidential Debates), they're not a function of government.

Callen, maker of mead and player of games, reporting in!
Are you using any chemicals, fermenting to dry and backsweetening, or are you letting fermentation stop naturally with excess sugars?

Thanks for the questions! Typically I like fermentation stop naturally. I take gravity readings of the must initially, and keep tabs on it until the gravity no longer changes. Once the gravity stays put for a while I sneak a taste and usually bottle around that time. I use champagne yeast, yeast energizer, and a crushed up campden tablet to keep things going and clean. Otherwise I keep my recipe simple as a semi-sweet mead.

However every now and then I like to enjoy a Cyser by adding several granny smith apples to the must after the first racking.

I'm still fairly new to the process, I started with 1 gallon batches and worked my way up to 5 gallon batches, all of which still have a slight yeasty taste, but still very enjoyable! If you have any tips, let me know!

don't campden tablets chemically stop the fermentation? I start with an OG of 1.114 and use Cote Du Rhones yeast (D47) and bentonite slurry to keep it clear. It ferments to semi sweet and only lacks acidty. I ferment on the lees, and no secondary necessary. My biggest batches were 40gals in stainless conical, but I don't do so much volume now that my province decides to tax it as a fruit wine.
